page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the instance in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is limited, as evidenced by weak multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, both falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block read and write bandwidth tests show average throughput, the Passmark memory score is poor, ranking in the bottom 10%. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, which contribute to average performance in encryption benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highcpu-4 offers a low-cost entry point into dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources, though it is constrained by its low memory density of 2 GB per vCPU. It is best suited for compute-bound workloads that require strong single-threaded performance but have modest memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded data processing, lightweight web serving, and basic utility scripting. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded compilation, or high-throughput web applications due to its lower multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth limitations.
